title: Mousepower: agents that can’t be measured, can’t be managed. — Maximillian Piras, Yutori
talk_summary: A founding designer at Yutori argues agents have a measurement problem: token spend is only an output and must be traced to clean outcomes, and the bottleneck has shifted from code generation to verification/review. He proposes a 2x2 'mousepower' matrix classifying tasks by uncertainty in execution steps vs uncertainty in acceptance criteria, favoring tasks that are easy to verify but hard to execute.

takeaways.technique: Task-selection matrix by execution vs verification uncertainty
takeaways.what_they_do: Classify each candidate agent task on two axes: uncertainty of steps to perform it, and uncertainty of the acceptance criteria; only automate the middle where steps are non-trivial but verification is cheap and repeatable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they become in this place where they kind of become the shape of an NP-style problem, which means they're easier to verify than to execute

takeaways.technique: Build the verifier agent alongside the worker agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat verification as a first-class deliverable: if you can find a repeatable verification pattern, deploy agents against verification too, not just execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't just build the agent, you perhaps build the agent that verifies the work of the agent

takeaways.technique: Trace tokens to outcomes, not token counts
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue token usage is an internal output metric; ROI requires cleanly tying spend to outcomes (bugs squashed, tickets closed) and then to objectives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tokens need to then be traced very cleanly to an outcome

takeaways.technique: Reserve frontier models for hardest tasks, change defaults
takeaways.what_they_do: Cites Coinbase changing default model choices so frontier models are used only for the hardest tasks, causing AI spend to diverge downward from token usage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they hadn't really started changing the defaults of what models they will start with and trying to only save the frontier models for the hardest tasks

takeaways.technique: Don't parallelize what you can't verify
takeaways.what_they_do: Frames parallel agent fan-out as token-maxing that only pays off if you can measure quality at the same speed as generation; otherwise the bottleneck just moves to human review.
